subject: Milestone slab & monthly thresholds — evaluation to commit timeline
messages:
From: Sam Reynolds <sam@atlasedge.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@atlasedge.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Milestone slab & monthly thresholds — evaluation to commit timeline

Hi Neha / Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at AtlasEdge is excited about the latency profile and the KV-caching savings you demonstrated. We pulled together a first-pass MAP (attached) and a proposed ramp. High level: we want a short, instrumented evaluation that can convert to a committed plan if we hit the acceptance gates.

Our proposed ramp (tokens/month):
- Month 1 (POC): 2,000,000 tokens
- Month 2 (integration + pilot): 6,000,000 tokens
- Month 3 (initial production): 18,000,000 tokens
- Month 4+ (scale): 36,000,000 tokens/month

We have a few asks:
- Can Redwood provide a staged discount ladder tied to monthly TPM milestones (e.g., larger discounts once we sustain >=20M/month)?
- Are there credits or rate guarantees if acceptance gates slip?
- Target close: we’d like a signed commitment within 2–3 weeks after POC acceptance (ideally by end of May).

Attaching: MAP_v1.pdf that outlines acceptance criteria and a simple SOW sketch. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate a faster ramp with a 30–45 day POC and a 60-day acceptance window? Also looking for ballpark effective rates so we can model econs.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Reynolds
Head of Platform Partnerships, AtlasEdge
sam@atlasedge.com

Attachment: MAP_v1.pdf (1.4MB)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam@atlasedge.com>, Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@atlasedge.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Milestone slab & monthly thresholds — evaluation to commit timeline

Hi Sam / Claire — great to get this over, and thanks for the clear MAP draft. We can absolutely support an accelerated evaluation with milestone-based pricing. A few notes / initial proposal below so you have something concrete to react to.

Proposed commit anchors (monthly tokens):
- Eval / POC (Month 1): 1,500,000 tokens
- Pilot (Month 2): 5,000,000 tokens
- Initial production (Month 3): 15,000,000 tokens
- Steady state (Month 4+): 30,000,000 tokens/month

Pricing / discount ladder (list price assumptions):
- List rate: $0.00060 per token
- Sustained volume discount: 10% when average >=5M/month for 2 consecutive months
- Mid-tier discount: 18% when average >=15M/month for 2 consecutive months
- High-tier discount: 25% when average >=30M/month for 2 consecutive months

Milestone credits / protections:
- If Milestone 2 (pilot acceptance) slips >14 days due to Redwood-provided infra issues, we will provide a one-time $30,000 service credit.
- SLA / latency credits are included in SOW for production traffic (details in SOW draft).

Map acceptance gates (suggested):
1) Infra smoke test & throughput validation (end of week 2)
2) Integration + sample traffic run (end of week 4) — acceptance required to trigger pilot pricing
3) Production acceptance (post cutover, 30-day window)

Next steps I recommend:
- We'll update the SOW and add the pricing ladder + credit language (attached as SOW_draft_20260420.docx).
- Proposed sign target: within 2 weeks after production acceptance to hit your end-of-May window.
- Can we book a 30-minute commercial sync on Thursday to agree anchors and finalize DocuSign routing?

If this looks directionally acceptable, we can bake Marcus’s commit-protection language (cc’d) and Jordan’s billing mechanics into the SOW.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Dir, Sales — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments: SOW_draft_20260420.docx (42KB)
From: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@atlasedge.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sam Reynolds <sam@atlasedge.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-21T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Milestone slab & monthly thresholds — evaluation to commit timeline

Thanks Neha — this is helpful. A few counterpoints from our side after internal review:

1) Discount level: to make the economics work for our customers, we need closer to 22–25% off list by the time we reach ~20–25M/month. 18% at 15M/month is a bit light.
2) Ramp timing: we can compress the POC/pilot to 30 days total if we get prioritized onboarding support from Redwood.
3) Credit for missed milestones: $30k is reasonable but given our go-live dependencies we’d prefer $50k as the remediation credit if Pilot acceptance is delayed >14 days and it materially affects our launch date.

If you can move to a 20% mid-tier discount at 20M and a $50k credit, we’re prepared to lock the MAP and route the internal procurement paperwork (DocuSign) within 10 business days after acceptance.

Two quick clarifying Qs:
- Can Redwood support a 60-day data retention window for audit logs on the pilot environment (we may need that for SOC review)?
- What’s the earliest on-call coverage you can guarantee during the 30-day production acceptance window?

Appreciate the flexibility — Claire
Claire Nguyen
Product Ops, AtlasEdge
claire.nguyen@atlasedge.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-21T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: AtlasEdge ask — pricing math and protections

Internal notes / recommendation:

- Pricing structure: convert the discount ladder into an effective committed rate for clarity. Example: if they reach 20M/month sustained, the effective rate at 20% off list ($0.00060 list) = $0.00048/token. For a 30M TPM steady state that’s an effective spend of ~$14,400/month at 30M tokens (math: 30,000,000 * 0.00048 = 14,400).

- Hybrid approach: propose a minimum monthly commit + overage tiers. That protects Redwood on unit economics and gives AtlasEdge a predictable effective rate. E.g., minimum commit 10M tokens/month for months 3–6, with overage billed at the discounted rate.

- Credits: $50k is large; recommend splitting remediation: $30k immediate credit + a $20k deferred credit that vests if they renew year-1. This reduces near-term exposure while showing goodwill.

- Operational asks: confirm 60-day audit log retention option (we can enable S3 export; security should sign off). Also confirm 24x5 on-call during the 30-day acceptance window (leader escalation path + named SE).

If we take the split-credit approach and commit-minimum + overage, we should be able to sign off. Marcus / Grace — please flag any billing or compliance blockers.

-Jordan
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@atlasedge.com>, Sam Reynolds <sam@atlasedge.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-22T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Milestone slab & monthly thresholds — evaluation to commit timeline

Claire / Sam — thanks for the clear counter. We can meet in the middle on a few points and keep the MAP timeline intact. Proposed compromise below: 

- Discount ladder (final):
  * 10% when >=5M/month sustained
  * 20% when >=20M/month sustained for 2 consecutive months
  * 27% when >=30M/month sustained for 2 consecutive months

- Credits: $30k immediate remediation credit if Pilot acceptance is delayed >14 days + $20k deferred credit applied at renewal if AtlasEdge renews for year-1 (split credit as Jordan suggested).

- Commit mechanics: 10M minimum commit/month for months 3–6, overage at discounted rate. This preserves unit economics while matching their scale expectations.

- Operational items: Redwood will enable 60-day audit log retention for the pilot and provide 24x5 on-call coverage during the 30-day acceptance window (named SE assigned at onboarding).

Next steps:
1) We’ll update SOW with the pricing ladder, split credit language, and commit mechanics — then route via DocuSign (link below).
2) If AtlasEdge confirms the compromise, we’ll target DocuSign routing tomorrow and aim to have signed MAP + SOW within 10 business days after pilot acceptance.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/companies/67890
